Rock of Ages isn't exactly the type of game that you'll become instantly attracted to after the first glance, but looking beyond that and getting to play it will most definitely change your impression. The words that describe this game the best would be somewhere in the area of a tower defense with two ends where your only attack option to help you reach your enemy's gate is your giant boulder, boulder that you control. The story mode puts you and your customizable boulder travelling through time and space, starting with ancient Rome and ending with the Renaissance era, fighting different characters from each time and location such as Leonardo da Vinci, Plato or Napoleon Bonaparte. There is no real difference between all those battles except for the map where the battle takes place, but the short, humorous animations that introduce the battle are a delight, as they make fun of anything and everything such as the moment when Leonardo da Vinci realizes that kids nowadays play with boulders in a video game created using "computieres". There are plenty of such moments and even though there is no actual plot to tie-in those battles apart from the fact that your boulder is inexplicably rolling from one battle to the next one after you've defeated your previous adversary, you can return to each one of them at any given time in order to collect the remaining hidden keys, improve your scores or simply because you wanted to have a quick laugh at one of those animations one more time. Choosing your character and your boulder is easy and intuitive, having a simple option in the main menu that allows you to select those and apply them to all the modes, including Time Trial and Multiplayer.
Rock of Ages was meant to be a tower defense game at its core, but that isn't the thing that makes it fun to play, as the boulder rolling mechanic will steal the show every single time you play. In theory a winning combination would consist of a valid strategy in tower defense in order to stop your enemy from reaching your gate and good boulder-controlling skills so you can get past your opponent's defences and crash into his gate, but that isn't exactly the case as for most of the times your defences will do nothing, but slow down your enemy's boulder for a bit and unless you're playing against the AI which is dumb enough to get stuck in random places at times, it is almost impossible for a human being to fail getting past any number of defences, so the game becomes more of a speed test, awarding the fast one to roll his boulder into the enemy gate, using the tower defense mechanic only to buy a few extra seconds. One more thing that influences the gameplay comes in the form of boulder power-ups, which range from the Angel Wings that allow you to perform one double jump to the Sun Upgrade which will deal considerably more damage if you manage to get to the enemy gate with your power-up still intact. After finishing the main story, you will definitely want to play against another human being as the AI's actions are predictable and there's no real challenge in defeating one of the animated characters one more time, and even if you do have all the maps from the story at your disposal in Multiplayer, matchmaking isn't as smooth as it could be, as you can spend entire minutes finding someone to play with and even when you do, it will become boring after a while since the fastest one on a map will always win.
The game is built using the Unreal Engine, which makes it a pretty thing to look at, but even so it is far from realistic and the physics can sometimes be weird, bouncing your boulder into a different direction. The crash effects are decent and the boulder damage, while not the best, does its job showing you what you did to your boulder after smashing it into all those towers. The level design on the other hand, makes things seem legit, as Rome will somehow look as you'd imagine Rome in miniaturistic style where boulders are supposed to roll for some reason.
There is no voice acting, but the sound effects and grunts that the characters make sell the ironic theme of the game and make those short animations fun to watch. The soundtrack might not be the best, but it is certainly fixed to deliver the background ambient that fits the on-screen boulder-rolling in each of the stages, making those levels feel authentic to the period of time and the location where each of those characters belong in real history.
The story can easily be completed within 5 hours, but afterwards you've got plenty of mini-games, reasons to jump back into the action for the missing keys and the Time Trial mode which will keep you busy for a few more hours if you want to achieve the gold medal for each one of the maps. The multiplayer, even with its issues can be a fun experience, especially if you find someone to play with for a longer period of time so you won't have to go through the matchmaking system after each match. Apart from the Online Multiplayer, the game also features a Local Multiplayer component which allows you and a friend to play all the modes in split-screen, however on the PC version you will need 2 controllers in order to do that, something that most of the PC gamers don't have, and considering the fact that the game only uses the direction keys, the game could have been easily played on the same keyboard.
Rock of Ages is fun and humours, so if you're looking for something different and with a healthy dose of parody humour, look no further, as this game will keep you busy for hours to come if you're digging its concept and you're willing to look past its flaws. There are limitations, without any doubt, and even with all the content package included in the game there was much more that could have been done, but for what it is, the game can easily keep you and a friend busy for an entire night, doing a bunch of different things and playing with the game's mechanics to try out new stuff.

This is by far one of my most favorite games of all time!  In fact I love the entire Borderlands series, including 1, 2, the Pre-Sequel, and even the Tales from the Borderlands.  It's very hard to find much wrong with anyone of the Borderlands games except for maybe the Pre-Sequel (which wasn't bad but just not as fun or replayable as the other games).  I shall now list some pros and cons of the game.
PROS:
-Guns, lots and lots of guns
-Awesome graphic style
-More guns
-Wonderful playable characters for different play styles as well as wonderful NPCs throughout
-Did I mention guns?
-Really fun and enjoyable combat that gets harder as you progress, and even lets you play through the game TWO more times with even MORE difficulty each playthrough...you know, if you like dying a lot and really challenging yourself by dying a lot and trying not to rage.
-Awesome loot based system that lets you farm for tons of cool different GUUUUUUNS!
-Amazing soundtracks
-Amazing DLC
-Multiplayer mode where you can play with random peeps online, or with your friends!  Nothing like that feeling of bonding while shooting some bandits in the face!
CONS:
-I think my one and ONLY con with this game is the loot system (which was also one of my pros).  While I love the random loot based system, it can be very hard to get the really good guns, sometimes even impossible in some cases.  Borderlands 1 loot system was much better.
Overall I freaking love this game.  I have more hours put into this game than any other game I own.  I HIGHLY recommend this game.

Borderlands 2 is a game that throws you in the deep end of the pool by getting you shooting up more things than you can imagine minutes after starting the story. It is recommended to play with friends for more fun and co-operation, however playing on your own is fine as the diverse characters and the funny things they have to say keeps you entertained all the way through. The leveling system is made to keep you at the right level during the game, so after 1 or 2 levels of grinding, you will not be getting much experience to level up at all, this could be a posotive or negative depending on the way you look at it. I have heard complaints of the games art style and more specifically the outlines, however this art style gives off the same vibe as the game itself, and the game was not made to be deadly serious, with you shouting commands to your friends, it was made to be fun and interesting, and that is what the art style delivers. The skill tree varies for each character, giving lots of replay value to the game to see what combinations of skills are possible to make the most powerful class possible.
The DLC for the game hase their ups and downs in some ways. The DLC's for the first time run-through are set at specific levels, which makes it hard for you to be at the right level for each of them as they vary a bit depending on your level, but only to a limitation. You can easily go over the recommended level by playing through one DLC and end up being over-powered on the the other DLC. However, these things aside as they are only really the first time run-through that it occurs on, the DLC offers new worlds to explore and hours of more interesting storyline, witty phrases, familiar faces (and some new ones) and fun to be had.
I strongly recommend this for someone looking for hours of fun with their friends, or on their own. Anyone who is skilled and wants to make a combination of skills that work together nicely in the skill tree, or fun someone just wanting to get stuck into a game.

This one was interesting enough. It felt like it was more of a challenge. The HOGS were well done in that some things were difficult to spot. The collectibles did not appear to be missable because you could return to all rooms until the end.
The bonus content was a bit silly and not important. It took less than an hour. The fast travel didn't seem to work in it. But it was short enough not to be a huge bother.

Game Mechanics:
The game consists almost solely of logic puzzles and hidden-object-scenes, though they are relatively well-designed they use, what is in my opinion, the single most unnecessary and time-consuming tactic ever: morphing objects. These objects morph between more than one form, meaning you will have to wait to cross the item off your list if you missed and just plain making them unnecessarily hard to find in the first place.
Plot:
The plot is pretty decent, though strives to be more epic and exciting than the mechanics of this game allow. The presure of time just doesn't feel as strict when you're lazily looking for irrelevant objects in someone else's mess.
Presentation:
The artwork isn't all that bad, but it feels kind of raw in places and could've used a bit more polish. The design in and of itself for both the areas and the hidden-object-scenes is pretty well done, if a little rough and the music is relatively atmospheric (but again doesn't really amplify the sense of urgency).
Completion:
If you've got this one, it's a pretty easy one to complete, just do it.

ADOM (Ancient Domains of Mystery)  is a roguelike adventure game, developed by a team of 5 people. This review is coming from someone who has not played the original games in the series and has no prior knowledge, and from someone who didn’t grow up playing this type of game either. Please bear that in mind with this review.
Gameplay is like any other roguelike game, where you get to choose from an array of different characters, and develop levels, statistics and skills as you progress.  The game is played from a top down angel and is very heavily weighted towards stats and what choices you make in whether you succeed or fail.  The game’s tutorial absolutely bombards you with way too much information which personally left more confused compared to when I first started. The controls and UI are quite possibly the worst I have ever experienced in a game too. There is quite literally a different button for every single mechanic in the game. This game made me feel sufficiently stupid because of how much jumble there is on any one screen at any time. The game was telling me to use buttons that I don’t think I have ever used on this keyboard. I am surprised this is one of the most popular roguelikes ever just from going off the usability of the game thus far.
The graphics are bad, there is no way around it and anyone who says otherwise is purely saying it from a nostalgia standpoint.  The pictures in the screen shots are definitely not what the game looks like on my screen, and I was playing the game in 4k.
I am still stuck in the tutorial of the game, because of being dumbfounded with the controls and the amount of information being thrown at me but this game if you manage to get into it, will offer you hours and hours of content with a very high replay ability factor also being the main reason behind this.
I am fully expecting this review to not be very popular given that I have reviewed it before even getting out of the tutorial; and I am clearly missing something about this game since it is so highly rated. But for me, having not grown up playing this type of game, and from someone who is not able to take in abundant amounts of information and learning the most whacky confusing control scheme, I simply cannot recommend it. It is possibly a generation thing, but if you mostly agree with my reviews and enjoy the same games I do, then you may want to eerie on the side of caution when trying this out as it is simply a game I did not enjoy at all.

ADOM is one of the 'Gods' of the traditional roguelike genre, starting as a MS DOS game in 1994, continually being  development to this day.  It features several dozen different dungeons, some with fixed layout and others randomly generated each time you play.  It also has an 'overworld' adventure map, which was an unique feature in ADOM's young days.
There are a lot of different character types you can make from a big selection of races and classes who can pursue multiple different endings.  Save the world from ChAoS as a Troll Paladin, or maybe take the place of the elder chaos god Andor Drakon as a Hurthling Farmer? Anything goes.
ADOM has always been and will continue to be freeware, downloadable from the developer site adom.de.  Recent features include the graphical Noteye tileset that vastly improves the visual appeal.
On Steam, the Deluxe version promises a slew of additional features, many of which at the time of this review several months after release have not been realized in the game.  This is a point worthy of critique.  The small development team working on ADOM have always done things in their own pace, which is perfectly fine for a freeware hobby project.  However with a Steam release comes expectations of promises being delivered on.  As much as I love the devs and the wonderful game they've created, this must be pointed out.  While ADOM is a complete game in its own right, the DELUXE version is far from complete.
That bit of complaining aside, ADOM is a beautiful game.  It is a brutal, oldschool roguelike with such a staggering depth that even with the community wiki on hand, it can take years to uncover all its tricks and secrets.  It will kill hundreds of characters, often just when you felt they were getting somewhere before you can even think about beating the whole game.  It has the replayability for the game to still be addicting to play for all those attempts, with all its character variations and random generated nature.  In fact, I recommend this game not for the story and reaching its ending, but for all the journeys your poor doomed characters embark on before they inevitably get crushed.
If you like turnbased dungeon crawling, traditional roguelikes with deep systems that you will keep learning new things in even after years of playing, ADOM comes strongly recommended.  However!  I would suggest playing the freeware version on adom.de first.  Unless you just want to support the developers of course (which you should!).  The Deluxe version of the game on Steam doesn't as of yet add much of features to justify a price tag.  Once implemented I think the Steam version will be safely recommended, as well.

This game is an instant classic. The RTS appeal to this game and the original Plague Inc. on iOS and Android was what brought me to this game. It provides a unique experience that can be enjoyed for a good 2 or so hours before it becomes repetetive, and several challenging disease builds and difficulty levels will also leave those who are dedicated with something to do quite a lost more time.
PROS:
- Unique and fresh, distinct from the rest of the RTS genre.
- Interesting gameplay, although repetetive.
- There is always a good healthy chance of losing on normal or above difficulty.
- Developer promises to continue updating game with new content with the most recent addon being the Neurax Worm.
- Slight sense of humor during gameplay.
- Not riddled with game-breaking bugs.
CONS:
- Limited replayability.
- Only minor gameplay differences between standard disease types (Goal is to extinct humanity every game).
- Early Access, not final product... yet.
- Not as hyper-realistic as advertized, it is realistic, but a more accurate geo-political map (Bigger and more specific) could have improved the overall gameplay, although in retrospect, the success of the gamey aspect of controlling the disease depends on a gamey and smaller map.
- Clearly an improved port of the iOS and Android version (you still have to pop bubbles to advance your DNA and stop the cure)
-A single music track replayed over an entire game
Overall, this is a solid early access game, while it has its faults (in my opinion), Plague Inc. Evolved has great potential for the future. To be honest, however, I am mostly looking forward to the new content and the Necroa Virus. I reccomend this game or those who have played the original and are strategy fans overall.
EDIT: I originally got into the original because of the flash game series Pandemic, such as Pandemic 2 which can be found at:
Also, there is significant Roleplay value in this game due to the original perspective of the game, along with new content such as the Neurax Worm and the Necroa Virus.

Having spent countless hours in other bethesda games like skyrim, oblivion, morrowind, fallout franchise, and doom I am sad to say this doesn't add up. The music is great! The world is not rendered the best but hey its a mmo and we want to target to as many people in one area that we can. What it should have is some sort of real theif system. It is a weak imitated version of what is found in the other games. Local economy really does not exist either. There is this guild shop system that is kinda there....and you can trade things there for the most part but a good ol auction house would have been fine. The crafting system is horrible and some parts are actually locked behind pay to clear time walls. So here we go into pay for advantages to further something in game over those who just play. There are the loot boxes in this game that can give you real game advantages that are almost gaming breaking. ESO plus membership gives you an advantage in small gold earned, in game currency, and access to all dlc while you are eso plus. Well that is a fat lie you do not get access to all dlc. There is alot you have to pay for. Calculated if you pay for all of say.....FF14 expansion plus the subscription its less than paying for the dlc and the over priced eso plus.
That all being said its hard to get behind this game for all its cash grab money fest that ESO is. PLus it really is just a better version of everquest and isnt even doing anything exactly new.  Oh yeah and get ready for the crashes that will come with owning the pc version of this game.
In the end if your looking for an MMO maybe shop around a bit more. Its obvious this game isn't going to change how they want to market it...and if you want to see THE WHOLE GAME you are going to have to spend spend spend spend. Do not let these people tell you otherwise there will be fan boys of this game but if you want purchase the game and actually look in the crown store and play over a few hourse of the game. In the end on a scale of 1 being the lowest and 10 being the highest I give this game one jello pudding cup.

This is a cool little short-story. It isn't really a game so much as an interactive narrative that tells the story of a very dark and horrible event. I would note that younger players should not play it for two reasons. First, if they understand the narrative, it's an extermely disturbing story. Second, this is a very slow paced, one might say "boring" game that most younger players are going to be uninterested in. Basically, the game constists of walking (very slowly) around a couple of dark rooms and reading notes left by someone that tells the story. There is a little simple puzzle solving in the form of figuring out passwords to open the doors, but all the answers are given to you in the notes.
Overall, I found it to be a very cool little short story. It is disturbing, but if you like psychological horror, it's well done. My only complaint is the walking speed is just a bit too slow, given how many times you have to walk back an forth between the two main rooms, it can get a little overly boring.

Fingerbones is as abstract and  disturbing as it is short in length. It is not your typical indie horror game. The game has a heavy, dark atmosphere that adds to the discomforting truth presented to the player.
--------------------------------------------------------------
Pros:
+ creepy and intriguing story
+ tense atmosphere
+ effective, still and silent enviroment
+ shocking message and revelation
+ effective, implicit storytelling
+ puzzles are relativley challenging but logical, tie well into the story
+ fitting background noise add to the horror
+ can be completed in one sitting (10-20min)
+ FREE
--------------------------------------------------------------
Cons:
- sluggish keyboard & mouse controls
- gameplay is coarse, consists of walking and reading notes (like 'Gone Home')
- backtracking is necessary
- graphics are very primitve
--------------------------------------------------------------
Summary:
The shocking truth of the story is slowly fed to the player through a series of notes. The atmosphere and theme is dark and disturing in a way that goes beyond the blood, disgust and violence of most horror games. The game shows the terrible thing that a man has done, who is free and not bound by any rules. (sshh don't tell feminists about this game)

This is exactly the type of videogame i have been looking for since 2012, after the release of the FANTASTIC psychological shooter Spec Ops : The Line.
Fingerbones is a different type of horror game. It isn't a horror game that uses cheap jumpscares to frighten you
Instead, Fingerbones uses your mind through different notes scattered around an environment that you need to read to uncover the secrets of the place you're in. At the beggining, you don't know who you are, where you are or what your purpose is. After reading every single note, uncovering every secret of this AMAZING but at the same time HORRIFIC
story, you finally find out who you are and what your purpose was from the beggining.
The game's main enemy is found right at the end, and this enemy will surprise you the same way as it surprised me.
The horrific story of the game somehow resembles I Am Legend combined with a Friday the 13th movie, although it's very original and the core is just a very tiny bit alike these 2 masterpieces.
Fingerbones can be finished in about 20-30 minutes, and uses no savegames.
Overall, all i can say is congratulations to the developer for creating this masterpiece. We need more games like these, games that make us think and eventually ♥♥♥♥ with our minds in both a good and a clever way.

To me, The Room the THE prime example of a "3D jiggsaw puzzle". As you cover the cornerpieces first. The picture will be more and more clear and you begin to understand the meaning of the art. Every piece you uncover leads into another one perfectly for what it does. The Room is not a game that discourages patience like many other puzzle games do. There is no time limit, no score, no competition to finish as quickly as possible, no heavy story that must be heard/seen. NB! The Story is optional to the game but not necessary to know. You're just in a room with a box in front of you, and you have to open it. That's the only objective. The game does have an eerie tone to it due to the setting being sometime around Victorian England. I would definitely reccomend The Room to people who appreciate what isn't looked at much like the setting, tone, music, style, approach from idea etc. This game will definitely not appeal to people who like action, adventure and other fast-paced genres. I wish only for the best to the developers to keep on making new puzzles and new installments in the franchise.

I absolutely love this game.  I got 100% on ps3, close to 100% on the older version on pc, and I plan on doing 100% again now for this version.  After an hour with the definitive edition I can already tell there are a lot of differences between versions, and I am happy to say so far they are all for the better.  If you are a fan of open world games this one should be at the top of your list of games to play.

After the 100% completion I can say that:
When it comes to visual differences the Definitive Edition features better lighting, character models and textures, some improved world textures, more depth of field, smoke, smoother reflections and visual effects. In short, the game feels more organic.
Now you have more people and cars on the screen. I've noticed new faces, different outfits and generally better looks.
The keyboard keys were remapped to more standard layout. Notable changes:
-RMB to E (entering cars, countering).
-Space to L.Shift (sprint and parkour).
-RMB now is used for lock-on.
The game mechanics are mostly the same. HUD has been slightly revamped, making elements sharper, smaller. Phone's front and UI has been changed completely. Most of the icons have been changed. Main menu has activity feed now and you can switch between social hub entries without the need to wait until they load.
The car traffic AI is okay-ish, heavy trucks still scratch the walls on turns, but I've noticed that the AI sometimes keeps crashing into my parked cars. Car physics are semi-buggy. There have been cases of weird spawns and semi floating vehicles.
Pedestrian AI needs a bit of polishing. I've experienced bunch of harmless / hilarious bugs and glitches:
-Some individuals keep walking into other people as if they were walking into a wall.
-Friendly AI had problems entering my car / locating door when needed.
-Some thugs were levitating for a brief moment.
-Panicking thugs tried to escape, got in a car and kept driving into a wall (they try to back off, but still hit the exact same spot).
-Enemy reinforcements sometimes get stuck between cars or they keep looking at you from afar.
-Random guy upstairs in Club Bam Bam went through the floor and landed on the ground floor like it was nothing.
-Some pedestrian animations keep overwriting themselves (loop too early) and end up looking like they're having a stroke.
-Sometimes people get spawned above the water.
-Some people get stuck in walls.
I've also noticed some audio issues. Sometimes some sound effects aren't played or they randomly appear / disappear. Seems like some audio bits also get either delayed or overlap (especially noticeable if happens during dialogues). Even had 2 radio tracks playing at the same time.
I'd like to point out that camera needs tweaking too. Sometimes it doesn't center well, stucks in things or points at wrong angles, has weird sensivity. Especially noticable in action hijacks.
I didn't experience these issues in original patched SD.
The DLC content is nicely implemented into the main game. You do not get instant access to the items (which would ruin the experience and challenge like in the original SD), instead you can access them in shops (the clothes guy says wacky lines about individual sets), so in-game currency has extra use now. The NANP and YOS side stories are available directly at the main menu, no need to switch between them. The red envelopes are now scattered all around the map and can be found in semi-hidden places. Notable difference: most of the DLC related side missions can only be played once, not including Zodiac island.
SWAT Pack DLC's unlimited side missions were turned into "Cop Job". No need to travel in a HKPD vehicles, the missions are marked separately on your map and unlock based on your progression. Possible scenarios (possible spoilers):
-You raid, beat up and arrest street gangs while having a bunch of officers as a backup.
-You're given a vehicle and have to ram the escaping suspect's car, then arrest him.
-You respond to store shootouts and neutralize thugs.
-Sharpshooting / one shot kill the thug without harming the hostage.
There are also some modified individual side missions (possible spoilers):
-"High Speed". Imagine Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit. You've given a police car and your goal is to shutdown a race by slamming into racer cars.
-Modified "Death by a Thousand Cuts". Arena fighting with a golden meat cleaver. Enemies have poisoned weapons and your goal is to survive and kill 30 enemies.  it's quite hardcore, especially if you haven't upgraded anything.
-Modified "Shaolin Showdown". Defeat 40 monks. Up to 30 on screen.
The optimization is even better than in the original. Playable on higher resolutions with less performance hits.
Notable difference: you can Alt+Tab freely. The game doesn't go into windowed mode anymore and stays in full screen, there's no need to change options back every time (which was extremely annoying).
Final verdict:
Worth if you've never (for some reason) played the game before.
Otherwise for fans that enjoyed the game.
PS. Needs a lot of patching. The bugs add up even if they're semi harmless.
I may update this review if we discover some new "facts".

Transistor is a beautiful game, from the art, world and music. It shows what it would feel like if you were inside the most fancients and most elegant of computer architecture. The is really cute with using computer jargon in it's gameplay and story elements. Such as not having enough memory to load all your functions. The story seems good, but is easily missable, the game emplores you to look for the story via reading the terminals and listening to your transistor blade. Where Transistor really shines is it's combat and difficulty. The combat is very unique while it is in real time there is a turn based element where you can unload a series of attacks simultaneous but doing so will leave you vulnerable to attack. So juggling between the turn based and real time combat is challenging and fun. The side missions which are the speed/perfomance/planning test are optional and quite fun. The planning tests I found the most fun, where you must defeat all the enemies in one turn. I would have like to see more tests and test variety. The games difficulty is dictated by limiters. Which are positive buffs to the enemies or negative buffs on you, you can decide how many are activate. The more that are active the more harder the game is. There is just enough different types of enemies to keep things fresh. I would have liked to see more creative boss battles as well as more of them. The game is quite short clocking around 4 - 5 hours if you're just doing the main story only. But it has a lot of replay value in it's combat and difficulty. Highly recommend if you are looking for a neo noir futuristic RPG which tries something new.

This game is an instant classic. The RTS appeal to this game and the original Plague Inc. on iOS and Android was what brought me to this game. It provides a unique experience that can be enjoyed for a good 2 or so hours before it becomes repetetive, and several challenging disease builds and difficulty levels will also leave those who are dedicated with something to do quite a lost more time.
PROS:
- Unique and fresh, distinct from the rest of the RTS genre.
- Interesting gameplay, although repetetive.
- There is always a good healthy chance of losing on normal or above difficulty.
- Developer promises to continue updating game with new content with the most recent addon being the Neurax Worm.
- Slight sense of humor during gameplay.
- Not riddled with game-breaking bugs.
CONS:
- Limited replayability.
- Only minor gameplay differences between standard disease types (Goal is to extinct humanity every game).
- Early Access, not final product... yet.
- Not as hyper-realistic as advertized, it is realistic, but a more accurate geo-political map (Bigger and more specific) could have improved the overall gameplay, although in retrospect, the success of the gamey aspect of controlling the disease depends on a gamey and smaller map.
- Clearly an improved port of the iOS and Android version (you still have to pop bubbles to advance your DNA and stop the cure)
-A single music track replayed over an entire game
Overall, this is a solid early access game, while it has its faults (in my opinion), Plague Inc. Evolved has great potential for the future. To be honest, however, I am mostly looking forward to the new content and the Necroa Virus. I reccomend this game or those who have played the original and are strategy fans overall.

Also, there is significant Roleplay value in this game due to the original perspective of the game, along with new content such as the Neurax Worm and the Necroa Virus.

ALBERT SCHLOSS! ALBERT SCHLOSS! I feel like I need to shout this from the rooftops! 5 stars just isn't enough for this place! It is by far one of the best bar/restaurants I have visited in Manchester for a while and I couldn't speak more highly of the friendly staff, warm and welcoming vibe and mouthwatering food, and here's why...
SO, I have visited here twice now - the first time just for a quick beverage which I enjoyed and really got a good feel for the atmosphere and bohemian bier palace vibe they're trying to get across. The place is HUGE but you can reserve a table/area with ease and the staff kindly greet you at the door and show you to your seats.
The second time I visited was to eat and celebrate my families Christmas! Sure we were already in good spirits but this places definitely lifted them to new heights.
We were quickly shown our table which was a nice booth at the back of the bar (slightly to big for a group of 5 but we made it work).
The waitresses came over quickly and took our drinks order. My mother and I opted for a bottle of their dry rose. We also asked a few questions about the menu as we weren't familiar with the German terms and again the waitress was polite and answered all our questions with ease.
We ordered our food and began to drink our wine. Usually I'm a sweet wine drinker but I really enjoyed their dry rose and would definitely recommend it!
Now to the food...Yey! We started by sharing the meatballs, ham and cheese croquets and the tomato and basil flat bread (yes we were hungry).
The meatballs you could tell are made fresh as they have that slight crumble to them and are mixed with a real hearty chorizo flavoured sauce. They literally melted in the mouth.
Now I know what you're thinking - ham and cheese croquets... Well don't underestimate them. The cheese has a slightly sharp taste and mixed with the ham it's the perfect combo. As you cut into them the inside just poured our. Devine.
The flatbread was also a winner - crisp, flavoursome and topping plentiful!
I also had a spoonful of Alex's beer and onion soup which was just packed with flavour! A real rich, stew like textured treat. I'd only recommend this however if you're really hungry and it is ridiculously filling and rich - you could have it as main!
Now to the mains (by this point we were getting full). I chose the beef house special. My gosh, was it good! The meat literally melted in your mouth and with the compliments of bacon lardons, potato rosti, and pickled cabbage in a red wine sauce it was a dish Albert Schloss should be truly proud of - a taste sensation!
I also have my mums pork knuckle a try - SO GOOD! The pork just fell off the bone.
We also ordered sides of sweet pot and normal chips which were thin, crispy and yummy. There was actually quite a delay with the chips and when they finally arrives the waitress couldn't apologise more informing us that the waitress had fallen and dropped them so they had to be done again! As an apology they wiped all the sides and the bottle of wine off the bill - what service?!?!
As I said at the start I cannot speak highly enough about this German beauty in the heart of Manchester! I urge anyone living or visiting Manchester to give it a try! You won't be disappointed!
And to top it all off they have push for prosecco buttons for all those who enjoy a glass of fizz... Or two!

"Fingerbone" is a nice little... I would call it "interactive shortstory" rather than a game, but I dont mean that in a negative way.
Technical stuff:
The graphic is similar to "Music Machine" (same dev), simple but atmospheric (for example due to the light and dust effects) - I uploaded a few screenshots if you like to have a look.
The game mechanic is very easy and pleasant, you move by WASD, look around with the mouse and interact with items by LMB. Thats it.
A little annoying was that you cant really come near any objects like tables or the like, you stop a meter (~3 feet I guess) away from it as if you walked against an invisible wall. But that isnt a big deal, you get used to it and it doesnt happen very often anyway.
What else? Oh the sound. Theres no voice acting. Your character stays silent and you have to read the notes you find yourself. But for me that wasnt a negative aspect - I liked the silence and found it matches this whole atmosphere perfectly. The backroundmusic could be better to be honest. I found it a little annoying after a while but the game is so short, that you are finished before it really starts to bother you hardly.
Content:
Well like a said, actually its kind of a short story. You find yourself in a bunker with no information who you are and what you are doing there and have to look around and find out what happend by reading short notes which you find here and there on the map (and that was it. In fact there isnt really anything more to do than reading notes. Thats what I mean by its a story, not a game). By finding new/more notes, the story reveals, till in the end you know who you are, why you are in this place and what happend there. The end.
Conclusion:
I liked it and would recommend it. But ONLY for people who like to read and games in which the story is more important than the gameplay (or even in which there nearly isnt any gameplay except moving around and reading). Its in this regard (or actually in many regards) similar to "Serena" - if you liked this game you will probably also find something you like in "Fingerbones". But if you expect more than a very short story to reveal by reading notes, if you want a game where you actually have something to -do- that effects your enviroment and so on, this game isnt for you.
But since its free and only takes you 20 minutes... try it.
[If you liked this game and want something similar but more complex, try "[
]The music machine[/url]". I can really recommend it.]

[SUMMARY]
For a game that is free to play, and has very little download time it is most certainly worth your time, if you got 30 minutes or so spare, download this game and play it. Do note if you are under the age of 13, that you need to think carefully before playing this game, because it might scare younger players, but to be honest do feel free to play it, and finish it. Totally recommend: 8/10.
[IN DEPTH REVIEW]
So, you still have your doubts huh? Well, I’ll explain why it is so great.
The storyline is so brilliant for an indie horror game, to be honest I hate horror games, but this, was something I actually enjoyed, it has no jump scares (although I did rush the game for the review, I may update it later if there is one, that I may have missed during rushing), and is purely driven about the idea of psychological horror, and that’s what makes it such a compelling storyline, and, despite the multiple chills I felt going down my back, I continued, because I wanted to see what would happen, and how it would end.
In terms of playability, it is, like most indie games, a pick up and play, the only thing that will make you think, is the complexity of the situation, and not which controls you need to press, the themes of this game is mildly concerning, (not going to spoil anything) and at the end, really makes you think about yourself, and if what your doing is right. I really struggled to get started on this review, purely because it keep returning to my mind, but, that is what the game is meant to do to you.
The game itself is quite a lot more serious than the clone of games being released every 3 weeks (*cough* Five Nights at Freddy’s *cough*), and is a ton better than whatever they are releasing, so before spending some of your hard earned cash, (or not so hard earned cash, I don’t know how you get money), why not give this a whirl first? Truth to be told, it has more entertainment value than You-Know-What.
My only complaint about the game would be that the game really could and should have been a great deal longer, the story and plot line has so much room for expansion, don’t get me wrong this game is good as it is, but an update or something to have more of a capitalisation upon the story of the characters (trying not to spoil here), as it was not really explained enough to really give to effective of a cliff-hanger, but is suppose, it is about the psychological effects more than the plot after all.
Addressing re-playability,  it looks the game that you might feel inclined to play and then play again immediately, or after a few weeks of intervals, because the story immerses you so well, (like I said room for expansion) that you really want to replay it, (after this review I’m probably going off to replay it, because it’s so good), but, to be honest, it doesn’t need to be replayed, however, if you got the time, replay it, because it’s like your looking through a completely different perspective, and maybe I would of get FNAF 2 if I had the ability to be the animatronics, but to be honest, it isn’t up my street anyway, (I hate jump scares, poorest way of adding tension, but I’m not a game developer, so what do I know?), but I’m getting off topic.
Next on my list is the graphics, and when I say what you expected from a game that takes barely any time to download, your answer would probably be not much, however, this graphics, enhances the game, and makes it more immersive, it feels older, making you feel it is more unknown the games you normally play, and considering the engine used was Unity free version, you can count me impressed. I think the creator could not be more right with this “It features a unique artstyle that combines elements of pixel horror with realistic lighting effect, which is intended to enhance the surreal atmosphere”. That right there is exactly what it does, the graphic make it feel more real, it makes the atmosphere feel as if it is happening with just you in control of the body, and that the body you control, is you, and you want to know who is this character, and what is he/she doing here? What relevance does it have to the story? How does the title fit in with all this? And that is exactly why you play this game past the opening moments, because you want to know the answer, and you are going to play through this game multiple times just to find out what is going on here. And that is the true beauty of an indie game like this.
Last, but most certainly not least, the music. This tune, fits too well for this game, the eerie sound of the tune fits in perfectly with the game itself, as if the music was made specifically for the game (maybe it was?) because it naturally makes sense for the sounds being played and the game itself, I can’t have any real complaints about this game, because, on all aspects, its indie developer’s dream, because it doesn’t appear to have any bugs, its well-made and fluid.
I really want to say how impressed I am by this, and I give kudos to the creator for such a unique and enjoyable game, that has changed my opinion on all horror games, and the genre itself, maybe I might get those games with lots of zombies and jump scares in it… No. This game is beautifully original, and is hand crafted to a perfect game, and is an absolute gem.
If you’re still not willing to give this game a go, then… I don’t know, maybe you just don’t like psychological horror, or maybe you’re on your phone or something, and you can’t download it yet, who knows, maybe you’re holidaying in Belarus, and won’t be back for a while.
So, in a nutshell, good game, well played. Sorry for any mistakes, I’m not fluent English, if you have any questions, or want me to review a game, add me or drop a comment on this, or my profile.
And on that bombshell…
Goodnight!

A great game ! It not only plays in the 80's it also looks and sounds like a game from that era. You play a border-officer of a fictional Eastern Bloc country during the cold war.
Your job is to check the passports of immigrants and to decide who to let in and who to refuse. What sounds pretty boring turns out to be a quite fun puzzle game mixed with some elements from adventure games. You have to compare travel documents with your regulations and look for failures. Over time not only the regulations become more complicated also you get more and more efficient in your job and learn what to look for. Everytime you find a deviation in somebody's documents you get some sense of achievement. When you make too many mistakes on the other hand  your salary will be cut short which will make your own survival and that of your family members harder.
The whole experience lasts 30 in-game days and it is kept interesting while confronting you with a lot of decisions - not only who to refuse and who to let in. Some of the game's 8-Bit graphics and sounds are quite iconic - e.g. the sound of the bulletin you get when you make a mistake. All in all this game tries something new and was definitely an interesting experience for me. Recommended to all open-minded gamers !

I was a fan of the original way back in the day, played it constantly. Wrote my own program to auto-backup the saves so I could cheat permadeath when I wanted to. I have played many dungeon crawl games, including Rogue, the OG of the genre. Out of them, this is one of the best.
A large open world (for the genre) full of quests and NPCs. There is plenty to do and see in ADOM as well as a large selection of Class/Race combanations. The mechanics are perfect. This game was created based on PnP rpgs like DnD, and attempts to recreate this as much as possible. There are a ton of hidden rolls, and many are refrenced in the text. The text really makes it feel like a tabletop rpg, well written and really sets the tone.
ADOM is also Random and unpredictable. You may die on the way to your first town, killed by enemies you stood no chance against, or kick down a door  to find a large demon ready to rip your head off. With permadeath on it is a hardcore dungeon delvers wet dream come true. This game is hard.
But now there are options to turn certain features, like permadeath, off. This opens the door for people like me, who enjoy the style, but dont like always playing a hardcore character. It also makes it easier to really enjoy the story and world without fear of losing your character . The graphics are not cutting edge, and I for one am glad. This is the update the game needed. Havent fiddled with the other game modes, but I theres just so much to do. I am also glad development seems to be continueing, so there may be more content to come.

Plague Inc. is not a highly complex game. It's a basic point and click with minimal UI options or perks. However, in sitting down to play it, I found it highly addictive. If you enjoy strategy and a good bit of reading, it's an excellent game. It takes a basic understanding of pathogens and a good bit of planning. Like chess, but with people and pathogens. As you complete scenarios you unlock different pathogens and genes to combine with them before starting your scenario. Once in game, the evolution process is fairly limited as far as evolution or upgrades. The game does have a few random events that accelerate or decelerate the spread or lethality of your creation which makes it interesting. The game AS IS, is really lacking, but still fun to play. Given how the Dev takes further development of the game, it has the potential to become extremely in depth. I definitely interested to see where things go. In the meantime, I'll be playing and trying to unlock all available mutations and genes. At $15 it's a little steep as far as what it is, but if you're a science buff / nerd / geek, in any sense of the word, it's still a must have. That being said, I see the true user base being limited, but for those that find the game appealing have great potential to become long term supports. I highly recommend watch an in-game video before purchasing.

Since a new update came out recently, I wanted to revise my review for this game after playing it for a lot more.
This game is still an awesome game and I have enjoyed it a lot more than most modern games I've played these days.
Pros:
Replayability
-Most areas are all randomly generated (save for a couple special places)
-Item drops and artifacts you get are random (you never no what you will get, good or bad)
-You can play the same character type again, and it will feel totally different from your first playthrough!
Tons of Content
-Many areas explore
-Plenty of quests to tackle
-Multiple endings (you can beat the game quickly or try and complete an ultra ending)
Customizability
-Many classes to choose from (ranging from easy to difficult in terms of playstyle)
-Many races to also choose from (you can be a Human, Dwarf, Elf, Drakeling, Orc and more!)
-The new point buy system is awesome and more improved! Make your fighter have lots of strength and toughness but little learning
-Different playstyles: You're wizard doesn't have to wear cloth robes only, have him wear plate armor and attack with weapons (assuming you got the strength for it ;))
Graphics/UI/Music
-The graphics and UI are very nice looking, especially after this update. The animations are nice as well, and soon there will character customization (I'm really excited for this one)!
-The UI updated also looks very good (although it does have a tendency to get in the way when your character is at the top of a map. Hopefully this gets fixed soon)
-The music has also been improved as well, and there are a lot of good tracks in this game
Support
-Game is still being supported years after it came out
-New content is planned even after this new update (new artifacts, levels, quests; Go check out the adom forums or the creators twitter for previews)
With any good game, there are also some cons:
Cons:
Difficulty
-When learning how to play, the game can be rather harsh (hunger, corruption, etc.). The difficulty barrier isn't as large as something like Dwarf Fortress, but it is there. You have to be able to learn from your mistakes. If you can't do that, this game might not be for you. If you stick with it though, it's a rewarding game.
-If you do have problems, the community is quite helpful (as long as you are willing to learn). There is an active adom community in the steam forums as well as in the roguelikes discord chat. Feel free to stop by!
-You can also turn off certain things like hunger and corruption, or you can also play with reloadable games if you want to play that way
Key Bindings:
-This game has so much in it, and there are a lot of key bindings that are somewhat unintuitive. If you might not be able to figure it out, it can be quite frustrating. The game does give quick hints now, so its helpful, but this complaint is one I see a lot from negative reviews, and I do agree with it.
Bugs:
-Like many games, there are always going to be bugs you run into, and ADOM is no exception. The game runs quite well, but every now and then you will run into something that might be a problem. If that does happen, be sure to submit a bug report, otherwise they wont be able to be fixed.
Tedium:
-One thing that I might complain about is there is a small amount of tedium in the game. You have be constantly eating, sacrificing for piety, managing inventory, avoiding cats, going to certain areas at certain times etc. It's not a huge deal, as imo it adds an interesting twist to the game. However, it might be a turn off for some people, so I thought I would just bring that up.
-A lot of knowledge can be found from the adom wiki, which is maintened quite well by the community.
Past these cons, I love this game, and would highly recommend it to anyone who loves roguelikes!

(i've played both the Steam and Android releases of Demon Hunter: Chronicles from Beyond, and this review applies to both.)
Like all Artifex Mundi releases, this game is graphically top-notch, with pleasing music and game-play targeting casual gamers. After having played some 6 of their titles, i can say that one thing sets this particular title apart from all others: almost every single HO scene uses at least one ambiguous term in their list of words. e.g., "bird" when there are _two_ distinct birds in the scene, "bulb" when there is both a lightbulb and a bulb of garlic, "necklace" when there are clearly two of them, and "hammer" when there are _three_ hammers in the scene. i.e., someone either didn't pay much attention during the HO scene design or someone set out specifically to annoy any OCD players. (i suspect it's the latter, given how prevelant this pattern is in the game (i've counted at least five scenes with this problem).) What does all that mean? It means that the chances of a hard-core player being able to achieve a misclick-free HOG experience is near zero.
It's a damned good thing i'm not OCD about this type of game. (OTOH, were it C code or software API documentation, i'd be flipping out _all over the place_, giving 37 different kinds of thumbs-down (thumb-downs?) and middle-fingers-up (middle-finger-ups?).)
That one point is my _only_ complaint with with this title. Yes, it's kitchy. Yes, it's casual. Yes, its lax use of ambiguous terms _will_ frustrate hard-core, OCD HOG players to no end. Nonetheless, it's a relaxing journey through yet another colorful Artifex Mundi environment, and i recommend it to any non-OCD players.
PS: once again a huge thanks to the developers for supporting Linux. Like all of Artifex's titles i've run on Steam, it runs flawlessly on my 64-bit Mint Linux 17.3 installation.
Post-completion notes:
- approximate play time of 5-5.5 hours (which seems about par for Artifex Mundi HOG titles). i started this on Android and moved over to Steam about halfway through, which deflated the total time reported by Steam.
- the ending felt somewhat anticlimactic to me.
- the three color-mixing puzzles made _absolutely no sense_ to me, neither the instructions nor the mechanics. i was forced to skip those.
- puzzles where turning a knob/wheel also moves a separate knob/wheel, screwing up any alignment made by prior rotation of that knob/wheel, just frustrate the hell out of me. Blood pressure shoots through the roof.
- the "item fades in and out" feature of a small subset of items in HO scenes is really rather annoying, as finding the item is less about finding it and more about stumbling upon it when it just happens to be in view.
- near the end the puzzles seemed to make less and less sense to me. e.g., where the mixing vials are hidden.

Since this game is a collector's edition it has some bonus contents. The contents: concept art, movie, wallpapers, music, puzzles, hidden object games.
There are total of six different trading cards. You only get the three of those cards from the game. There are several ways to get the rest of the trading card: Purchased from Steam's Market; Trade with friends; Booster Packs and it's Booster Pack Creator.

Just finished the game yesterday and this game got me mesmerized from the start to finish. Note : I do not understand Starcraft and frankly I did not play this game to understand SC2, I only played because I waanted to have an insight about the life of a professional eSports player, so I will not talk about the SC2 aspects in this review.
Well anyway, here goes my review :
This game tells the story about Mach, a foreign player from the West (maybe USA) who came to Korea to 'play Starcraft' and go professional. Throughout the course of the game, it told you how a professional eSports player creates a team and how they interacted/practised with their teammates (the game mainly focus on this), how the players' emotional condition affects their motivation, and what was required to succeed in eSports asides from talent and skill. I really think the game captures and retell those moments to the player perfectly and I do believe these process were similiar to some (if not most) professional eSports player's experience, I think it really gives you insight about competitive gaming life and how uneasy it is to live as an eSports player.
However, the game is not without it flaws though. There were moments that the game made seems very easy (which I was sceptical) :
1. The first was when Mach got scouted by Accell a renowned pro player. He instatenously agreed to play against him after watching him played one game, oh boy how would I love to be able to got scouted so easy like that and become a pro player also :O
2. Accell, Jett, Stunt and Reva seems to settle in with their team very quickly and looked very motivated. They literally became 'close friends' who trusted each other within one week since the team were established. Trust me, it is very rare to find a player who is not only skilled, but motivated and full of commitment, let alone being able to trust each other within that short amount of time.
All in all, it is a good VN that worth reading and you would not regret trying it out since it's also free. Like the others reviewer stated, I too would gladly pay for any sequel the devs may release in the future. I highly recommend this game.

This game, this game. OMG, even if you are not into visual novels. Heck, I barely play visual novel games, this is my 5th, heck I barely even write review, but I loved this game. You should really try this out. Trust me, you will have some trouble moving yourself away from your spacebar when you try to stop.
Its worth sacrificing 3 hours for this if your bored, especially since time is the only thing it will cost you. There is a good reason that this VN is in the top 5...

TL;DR I'd pay for a sequel, WHEN they start accepting any donations for it. *fingers crossed*
Gameplay: It's a visual novel, press SPACE or ENTER to proceed. Use the scroll-up mousewheel to view text if you accidentally skip it. The choices don't have much impact save for a few 'dead ends' but judicious use of their save system makes this a minor gripe at best and allows you to view the different 'routes'.
Story: For a visual novel, you'd expect this to be pretty damn important. Good news, it is. The characters are likeable, the 'villains' are detestable, and everybody has something at stake. The sacrifices they made to pursue their dreams rings true with me, and helps me cheer the main character (you) and his team on to victory. All their suffering, all their flaws, turns them into real underdogs that are desperately clawing for a dream where they may achieve happiness and validation in their lives. There are also bits and pieces of South Korean culture mixed in there plus a helpful glossary for terms about SC2 e-sports that you may not know at first.
Music: Background-variety music, sets the right mood, gets the job done, nothing spectacular here. Don't expect Hans Zimmerman-levels of epic quality.
Graphics/Art: Passable. The characters look nice enough although the girls really look like the guys, and makes me wonder if they cut corners by making male characters first then 'rounding them out' giving them slightly more hair to make them into girls. Most of the backgrounds are re-used, and not surprising for a game that is free.

This game was very difficult for me to review considering I went back and forth on my favour towards it so rapidly. Overall it’s an average game with some redeeming qualities like the unique mechanics and the arcade mode
Tl;dr version is: okay story, decent gameplay, absurd difficulty
~~ DIFFICULTY ~~
This is a very difficult game. And I know immediately upon reading this a swarm of basement dwellers will come at me going “it’s not difficulty; you’re bad at video games; go play Skylanders you baby” and other stupid parroted rhetorics. First, yes the game is difficult. Dark Souls level difficult, but on top of that stupid difficult. There are two kinds of difficulty: the smart kind where AI is smarter and senses your moves better requiring actual tactics, and the stupid kind where enemies are bullet sponges, there are hoards of enemies, and you die after 2-3 shots. This game does the latter. Enemies often appear out of nowhere (following the narrator’s dialogue) making you often unprepared and you’ll often die that first time on ambush. Second, their shots kill you in 2-3 hits often. Third, there are cases in boss fights where there is an absurd lack of cover. I remember fighting this shotgunning boss who kills you in two hits, and you have NO cover except a small wooden log which is useless because it’s a very small arena anyway. At least 50% of my deaths were there as I basically hopped around the level like a kangaroo stepping on Lego trying to shoot the guy dozens of times and then pray that I don’t die during reload sessions as he barrages you with bullets. No cover, swarms of enemies in all directions, and limited health make this game frustrating. I love difficulty when it’s done right. Dark Souls is good, XCOM’s crazy strategizing is good, Halo on Legendary is good. Making enemies bullet sponges, taking away cover, and swarming you: not good. This isn’t helped by the fact that the AI is really bad, standing in spot or in the open 1990s DOOM style. If you take cover they’ll never run at you and just shoot the seam of the wall you hide behind endlessly. The AI is really really bad.
~~ STORY ~~
Silas Greaves is the protagonist on a revenge mission. Pretty standard cut and paste plot point if you ask me, but it’s well executed. I really enjoyed how you were playing out the narrator’s storytelling, where the world is changing before you. It reminded me of the Borderlands 2 DLC. Really unique. However this was both a positive and a negative. Sometimes in the heat of gunplay you cannot pay attention to dialogue, making you miss important clues in the game, or not catching story elements.
~~ GAMEPLAY ~~
Standard cut and paste first person shooting: right click to aim, left click to shoot with a couple cool unique features like focus and death sense which allows you to sense a bullet right before it kills you and dodge it (then this sense takes time to recharge, so it’s not like it’s easy to avoid death). There aren’t that many weapon varieties and I found myself using only the rifle as it was the most reliable. There are insane frustrations too, like how sometimes you can shoot someone point blank and it will not register the impact. The best part of this game is by far the arcade. It’s an action shooting level reminiscent of, well, arcades. Blow through carbon copy enemies fast and try to earn high scores by combo kills and even some environmental damage with explosive barrels. I absolutely love the Arcade component. It’s a great way to blow off stress after work or if I only have like a half hour of game time.

Transistor is... interesting. I was sucked in by the number of potential combinations of combat abilities - and then I stuck around for the beautiful artwork and atmosphere of the game.
Transistor is an orthogonal view RPG - similar to those of the early 2000s. It's not standard, though: you don't have a party of multiple characters, and you don't have conversations with NPCs (or at least, not as such). Combat occurs in bounded areas, which you can't leave until finishing the combat - but your character can move freely within these. Abilities can be used in real time, or planned out using a "pause" kind of ability (which has to recharge after being used), making the combat more turn based and strategy focused.
There are three main things however, which really make the game shine.
First is the mystery/detective style story. The game starts with your character right in the middle of things, with very little explanation - and as the player, you spend the game trying figure out what happened and what exactly is going on. I found this to be a great storytelling technique, and very quickly got me hooked. Little snippets of information are "fed" to you through by your narrator companion; you also find various clues as you explore.
Another way of finding information is cleverly linked to the second notable thing about this game: the combat abilities.
As you progress through the game, (and level), you receive abilities called 'Functions' (a computer programming reference). Each one can be used as an active ability, set as a passive bonus, or used as an upgrade to your active Functions. This means that each new function you gain can have 3 different effects - and there are then an almost limitless number of potential combinations. The best thing about this though, is that you can freely change how you combine your Functions throughout the game. If something's not working for you, change it up. You can use one set-up to be effective against large numbers of weak monsters, and then change again for the boss battles. If you think a particular combination of Functions might be cool, fun - or even just good for a laugh - try it out, and you can always change again later. This encourages improvisation and experimentation, while also removing the pressure of making the right decisions on how to upgrade your character (which sometimes detracts in other games).
The Functions also tie in with the game's backstory. Each one is named after a character (including the one you control), and as you use the Function in different ways, more information about this character is available to read. This acts as another incentive to change around your Function combinations by slowly feeding you more of the story.
Finally, the whole atmosphere of the game really is something to experience. The character portraits and cutscene artwork are amazing, the way the protagonist hums along to the soundtrack of the game... I'm not sure what else to say - you have to see if for yourself.
Only a few complaints:
I found the combat to be a bit of a grind as I neared the end of the game (though that may just be me).
I also thought everyone's praises of the soundtrack were overrated, and left me disappointed. Ashley Barrett's vocals *are* stunning - but although the the music fits the environment of the game, it's just repetitive and mostly forgettable.
If all that leaves you wanting to know more - go play it! Why are you still reading this?
However, if that doesn't grab your attention, and you prefer your games to be a bit more standard with an overt story that starts more slowly - this one isn't for you.

Rarely do I review a game, but I feel in this instance I must.
theHunter is the best hunting sim out there. This alone demands that a certain demographic -- those not looking for a hunting arcade shooter where animals pop up every ten seconds -- take notice.
Yes, it costs for a yearly license to shoot every animal in the game. And yes, there are new free animals available for hunt, rotated every two weeks. My suggestion to a new hunter just starting out would be to find what animals are free, then go after them to see if you like the game enough to pay fora  license.
And yes, weapons cost money, as do callers, clothes, and everything else in the game. This is a part of what makes it a great game, in my opinion. There's a sense of ownership and challenge when you purchase a new weapon and bring it out into the field. Leveling up a weapon is actually fun when you know you've just paid for it. I've been in the game for years now and do not own every weapon in the game, nor do I need to: I've had a blast leveling up the ones I do have, and I am nowhere near to mastery with any save the pump shotgun.
To trash this masterpiece because of its aggressive business model is a real shame. For my part, I am happy to continue to support the devs with my money because they're constantly adding new things.
Bottom line: if you want a hunting sim, here's the best available to you.

This is the hunting simulator I've been wanting for years, and you can love it too, if you keep a few very important details in mind:
1. Despite its claims, this game is not really free to play, or at least, the free to play model is not great. To really enjoy it you need to invest a good $30-$40 to get some good equipment (so you don't scare every animal away immediately) and licenses (so that you can hunt any animal).
2. This is NOT an arcade-type hunting game. It actually requires you to hunt, tracking your prey and occasionally losing them. It takes time and patience. There will not be ten bucks popping out at you every five seconds. This is actually what I love about the game, but I can see how some would not take to it as easily if they were expecting something else. Besides, the world is gorgeous. Take time to walk and enjoy the sights along the way. Pro tip: After the first 150 yards or so after leaving your hunting camp, don't use the run button. It can scare the animals away. Again. you have to be able to enjoy a slower-paced game.
3. The user interface takes some getting used to. It doesn't work like your average first-person shooter, and there is not a great tutorial that teaches you everything. Most of your important items, like your weapon and deer call and such are mapped to the number keys. Watch a beginner's guide on Youtube or on the TheHunter wiki page before diving in.
If you can handle those three things, you are in for an incredible hunting simulation. The slower-pace makes the successful kill incredibly satisfying, and the online tournaments you can enter (you don't play with other people; just submit your best kills to see who scores the highest) add tons of incentive to keep playing. As I said, part of the joy of this game is just enjoying the world. I don't know how many screen shots I've taken during my time in-game. It's beautiful. Happy hunting!

Borderlands 2 - One of the best games that I've ever played.
Borderlands 2 is the absolute epitome of an open-world RPG shooter. A GOOD open-world RPG shooter. This game is so marvelous and fantastic that I don't even know where to begin with this game. The story is pretty straight foward. You're Vault Hunters, you almost get killed by the main villain named Handsome Jack, and you're on your journey to stop him. However, the main story isn't what makes the game in my opinion, it's the side missions and the co-op.
You get to play as many different characters, each one having their own special abilities, which brings great fun.
I've been playing this game with my friends and I must say, it's a splendid experience. I've always had my doubts on online co-op story games, but man was I wrong. Plus, the flexibility is so beautiful that you'll still enjoy this game with up to four friends, and then all by yourself. The only issue that I can think of in this game is that the game can get a bit tedious if you're underleveled against higher level enemies, but then again, you can always level up by doing side missions or collecting items.
And there's so much more that I haven't discussed in this review, such as the sensational combat system, level up system, loot collecting (my favorite part in the game), and so, SO much more! Pick this game up if you wanna pour hours and hours and hours of never ending fun and enjoyment. I give this game a 9/10.

When I went into this game, I expected it to be sort of like Katawa Shoujo, but with StarCraft, and less sad. Instead, what I got was genuinely good writing, with good visuals, and a great story. As a fan of eSports, it was interesting to get insight into the more human aspects. Let me break it down a bit.
The writing. It was really good. Characters were believable and likeable. The dialogue conveyed what was meant to be brought across.
The visuals. The game looked nice. I'm somewhat a fan of the style used here, and the backrounds looked great.
The story. Without giving away too much, it follows a upstart SC2 player who travels to South Korea in hopes of making it big in the pro-gaming scene. It was really interesting, and I found myself invested in what it told. One complaint though is that it was over a bit fast, and the ending leaves a bit to be desired. However, a sequel is apparently a possibilty, so I hope that is the case.
Overall, this is a surprisingly good game, and I definitely recommend it to fans of VN's and really anyone who looks for a good narrative.

pretty solid game, fun and satisfying shooting with a decent story.
The shooting is the highlight of this game. Cool matrix-like bullet time, hardly any tanky enemies, mostly everything dies in one hit with a headshot so you can feel pretty badass running through an area dodging bullets and killing gangsters with well time slo-mo shots.
In terms of story the game is okay. the story is told in a unique way so I give it some bonus points for that. They story is narrorated a drunk story teller speaking to some fellow bar patrons. This is cool because the diolouge between the storyteller and his audience is great way of providing exposition without it seemming out of place. another cool thing with the way the story is told is sometimes you see the levels and events get drawn in around you as the narrorator describes them.
There are some collectibles throughout the levels, a decent selection of guns, and three skill trees that the player progresses through throughout the story.
My only real complaint is that the game has black bars at the top and botttom of the screen. they can be ignored after a little adapting to them, but they are there nonetheless.

I don't like giving negative reviews to an Artifex Mundi game since their works are usually the best, but I would recommend this one only to Hidden Object Games' novices, not so much to expert players. The graphics are good and there's an extra chapter after the main story, but It's very easy even at expert difficulty and the story is weak compared to other Artifex Mundi titles. The only slightly difficult thing about this game is getting some achievements (like finishing certain puzzles at the first try), other than that I was very disappointed.

Another competent hidden object game that is perfectly playable and easy to recommend as long as your expectations aren't too high.
Overall the story is decent enough but fairly predictable and sparse, and fairly random/illogical at times - for example the way of rescuing the clock hand from the fountain, or the way you use lightning and then immediately stand in the very recently electrified puddle while the storm continues to do a hidden object scene, etc.
The English translation has a number of mistakes, but luckily nothing that really affects gameplay much (cigarette bud confused me for a few seconds, and it took a while to get used to looking for a compass when asked for a divider, although I think in this case it is technically the correct term for the tool, but rarely called by this name at least in British English outside of specialist circles). The voice acting is fairly decent, although there isn't a whole lot of it - and mostly it is your protagonist narrating events in cut scenes.
In terms of gameplay the point and click sections are all okay, if prone to fairly random events happening, the puzzles are all okay but very easy, and the hidden object scenes are fine apart from the weird morphing thing where objects you need to collect turn into something else you can't click on for a short while. This can attract your attention to the movement on screen (but 50% of the time to something you can't collect) or make you think you have checked an area when you have actually missed it, I am not sure this really adds anything, it just sort of randomizes how difficult scenes are a bit. The standard map with teleport and pointers to where you can do stuff is included, which is always a plus especially in games where you jump around between locations over and over as you do here.
The extra chapter in the collectors edition is pretty well done and atmospheric, although the puzzles are a bit repetitive (in the 7 or so rooms in it, you do the 7/5 capacity beaker thing you already did in the main game right at the end twice more for example), and given the amount of running back to the first room that happens later on it is annoying the map teleport is turned off for the bonus chapter.

This is another decent Artifex Mundi contribution to the genre and while it has many familiar aspects of an AM game, it's not the most stellar addition to their library.  However, despite some shaky plot (or lack thereof), it has all the HO and minigame love that fans of the genre will appreciate.
Sound and music is done well enough.  Nothing that stands out and nothing that's terrible.  Graphics look nice enough for the game type.  Animation is minimal but decent, especially the final scenes.  HO scenes are detailed but not challenging.  The game adds "morphing" objects that can only be clicked when the in correct form; this would be irritating except for the quite fast change time which means you won't have to wait more than a couple of seconds for it to flip back.  If you don't have the patience to wait five seconds, you may not like it.  I didn't mind.
My single grouch with the game is the lack of plot; there's some good setup, then a lot of not-much, until the very end when you get a chunk of information sort of tossed at your head.  But even that information is scanty, and not in a "you have to roll it around in your brain to make a conclusion" awesome way.  I'm hoping the bonus chapter has some more back story but it honestly should have been in the main game.
The game time isn't terribly long, so like most of these games, I recommend waiting for a sale.  It's running about two hours for the main game (I haven't done the bonus content yet).  With the short playtime and sketchy plot, I wouldn't get it full price.  But with a sale, I wouldn't hesitate to grab it.  It's a fun playthrough even with the plot issues.
